title: North Carolina's 9th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for North Carolina's 9th Congressional District pits seven-term Republican incumbent Richard Hudson against Democratic nominee Richard Ojeda, a retired U.S. Army Major and former West Virginia state senator. The district, which covers parts of Alamance, Chatham, Guilford, Cumberland, Hoke, Moore, and Randolph counties, was redrawn under a new Republican-drawn map enacted in October 2025. Cook Political Report rated the race as 'Solidly Republican' ahead of the primaries, but Democrats see Ojeda's military background and populist message as potentially competitive. Hudson serves as chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee (NRCC), making him a top Republican strategist and fundraiser for the 2026 cycle.

candidates.name: Richard Hudson
candidates.summary: Richard Hudson has represented North Carolina in Congress since 2013 (8th district until 2023, 9th district since 2023) and serves as chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee, making him the fifth-ranking House Republican in leadership. He serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and is a recognized conservative leader focused on cutting federal spending, reducing drug prices, and supporting military families. Hudson holds a BA in political science and history from UNC Charlotte and previously worked as district director for Congressman Robin Hayes and as campaign manager for Pat McCrory's gubernatorial bid.

candidates.name: Richard Ojeda
candidates.summary: Richard Ojeda is a retired U.S. Army Major who served 25 years in the military, earned two Bronze Stars, and spent much of his career at Fort Bragg, North Carolina. He served as a West Virginia State Senator from 2017 to 2019 and ran briefly for the 2020 Democratic presidential nomination before moving to North Carolina. Ojeda won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary for NC-09 with 41.8% of the vote, campaigning on a platform focused on veterans' issues, working families, and healthcare. He holds a BA from West Virginia State University and an MBA from Webster University.
